basis: Epilepsy and speech dyspraxia define a neurologic disorder; intellectual disability and language impairment share this axis.
Benign blood-vessel neoplasm arising in the skin.
Malignant tumour involving the kidney; other metastatic sites are not intrinsic to this umbrella concept.
Premature fusion of cranial sutures defines the disorder; additional organ disease varies across syndromes.
Chronic immune-mediated airway inflammation and variable airflow obstruction define asthma.
Autoimmune skin blistering; oral lesions occur in <30%. Diabetes and recurrent infections do not establish direct damage by pemphigoid.
Infection occupies the cranial or spinal epidural space and can compress neural structures; associated osteomyelitis is a separate disease.
Disordered epidermal keratinization; ancestors and subtypes identify a skin disorder.
Delayed endocrine maturation with transient hypogonadotropic hypogonadism; delayed skeletal maturation does not establish bone damage.
Hereditary motor and sensory peripheral neuropathy with abnormal myelin folding.
Cassava-associated neurotoxicity causes persistent motor pathway or peripheral nerve dysfunction.
Localized cutaneous amyloid deposition with progressive pigmentary lesions; systemic amyloidosis is explicitly absent.
Inherited epidermal keratin disorder causing skin fragility, blistering and subsequent hyperkeratosis.
Malignant T-cell lymphoma; no particular extranodal organ is consistently affected across this histologic variant.
Prototheca infection; direct cutaneous infection accounts for roughly 50–70% of cases. Olecranon bursitis generally occurs in <30%.
Cardiac sodium-channel disorder causing prolonged ventricular repolarization and potentially lethal arrhythmias.
Diaminopentane excretion suggests an inherited metabolic handling abnormality; sparse supplied information does not establish renal injury.
Meningeal tumour with sphenoid bone infiltration/hyperostosis in most; orbital involvement causes visual or ocular motor dysfunction in >30%.
Localized tongue depapillation and glossitis, usually representing chronic oral Candida infection.
Inner-ear dysfunction causes sensorineural hearing loss and vestibular attacks; vertigo does not imply central neurologic damage.
Nonsyndromic progressive sensorineural hearing loss; no additional organ involvement is established.
Treated refractory plasma-cell malignancies are predominantly myeloma; bone lesions affect most and renal impairment about ≥30% over the course.
Inherited intrahepatic bile-transport disorder causing progressive cholestatic liver injury; MYO5B-associated intestinal disease is a distinct phenotype.
Camptodactyly, joint contractures, clubfoot and facial skeletal dysplasia define a skeletal and joint disorder.
Benign tumour of breast ducts; breast tissue lies outside the thirteen axes.
